assessments.note: The card's 'last European country to allow divorce' is wrong for Ireland 1997: Malta still banned divorce until 2011. Ireland in 1997 was the last member state of the then European Union; wording narrowed and body corrected.

support.quote: Before Monday's vote, Malta was the only EU state without divorce legislation.

assessments.note: Context: after Ireland's 1997 law, Malta (EU member from 2004) was the only EU state without divorce, so Ireland in 1997 was the last EU member of its day to allow it, not the last European country.

support.quote: the bill was written into law in 1996 and was due to come into effect on 27 February 1997
Family Law (Divorce) Act, 1996
Before Monday's vote, Malta was the only EU state without divorce legislation.

The staunchly Catholic island of Malta was yesterday set to end its status as the only European nation that does not allow divorce after a narrow "Yes" victory following a bitterly fought referendum campaign.
Legislation introducing divorce came into effect in October 2011 following the result of a referendum on the subject earlier in the year.
The Netherlands' gay community rejoiced with tears and whoops of exultation Sunday over the world's first same-sex marriages recognized under a new law.
We're the first country in the world where there is no distinction made on the basis of gender.
Four gay couples have exchanged wedding vows in Amsterdam's City Hall under a new Dutch law that recognises their civil marriage.
In 2001, the continental Netherlands became the first country to broaden marriage laws to include same-sex couples.
In 1989, Denmark became the first country to legally recognize a relationship for same-sex couples, establishing registered partnerships
Elsewhere in Europe, Norway and Sweden allow gay couples to register their partnership whilst Denmark was the first country to allow gay marriages in 1989.

assessments.note: BBC loosely calls Denmark's 1989 registered partnerships 'gay marriages'; the year and the first-country claim match.
